ko.title: 빅테크의 새로운 건설 자금 조달법: AI 열풍 뒤에 숨은 채권 빌

segments.src: For most of the past two decades, the defining financial fact about America's largest technology companies was how much money they had lying around.
segments.tr: 지난 20년의 대부분 동안 미국 최대 기술 기업들을 정의하는 가장 명확한 재무적 사실은 그들이 보유한 현금이 얼마나 많은가 하는 점이었습니다.

segments.src: Cash piles measured in the hundreds of billions became a running joke on earnings calls and a genuine policy question in Washington.
segments.tr: 수천억 달러에 달하는 현금 더미는 실적 발표 전화회의에서 단골 농담거리가 되었고, 워싱턴에서는 진지한 정책적 의문이 되었습니다.

segments.src: The companies were so liquid that the main debate was what to do with the surplus: buy back stock, pay dividends, or park it offshore.
segments.tr: 이 기업들은 유동성이 너무 풍부해서 주된 논쟁거리는 잉여 현금으로 무엇을 할 것인가였습니다. 자사주를 매입할지, 배당금을 지급할지, 아니면 해외에 두어야 할지 말입니다.

segments.src: That framing is quietly going out of date.
segments.tr: 그러한 프레임은 조용히 시대에 뒤떨어진 것이 되어가고 있습니다.

segments.src: The build-out of artificial intelligence infrastructure has turned the most cash-generative businesses in the world into some of the largest borrowers in the corporate bond market — not because they are short of money, but because even their extraordinary cash flow no longer covers the bill.
segments.tr: 인공지능 인프라 구축으로 인해 세계에서 가장 많은 현금을 창출하는 기업들이 회사채 시장에서 가장 큰 차입자 중 일부로 변모했습니다. 이는 그들에게 돈이 부족해서가 아니라, 그들의 특별한 현금 흐름으로도 더 이상 비용을 감당할 수 없기 때문입니다.

segments.src: ## The scale of the spend
segments.tr: ## 지출의 규모

segments.src: Estimates compiled from company guidance and analyst models put combined 2026 capital expenditure across the major hyperscalers at upward of **$750 billion**.
segments.tr: 기업 지침과 증권사 분석가 모델을 종합한 추정치에 따르면, 주요 하이퍼스케일러들의 2026년 합산 설비투자(capex)는 **7,500억 달러**를 넘어설 것으로 예상됩니다.

segments.src: To put that in perspective, it is a figure that would have described the entire capital spending of the S&P 500's industrial sector not long ago.
segments.tr: 이 이해를 돕자면, 얼마 전까지만 해도 S&P 500 산업 부문 전체의 설비투자 규모에 해당하는 금액입니다.

segments.src: The more revealing number is the ratio.
segments.tr: 더 많은 것을 시사하는 숫자는 비율입니다.

segments.src: That spending represents roughly **94% of the group's operating cash flow** — meaning almost every dollar these companies generate from running their existing businesses is being committed to building the next one.
segments.tr: 이 지출은 **이들 그룹 영업현금흐름의 약 94%**에 해당합니다. 즉, 이 기업들이 기존 사업을 운영하여 벌어들이는 거의 모든 달러가 다음 사업을 구축하는 데 투입되고 있음을 의미합니다.

segments.src: Historically, big tech converted operating cash flow into free cash flow at a comfortable clip, leaving ample room for buybacks and dividends.
segments.tr: 역사적으로 빅테크는 영업현금흐름을 상당한 비율로 잉여현금흐름으로 전환하여 자사주 매입과 배당을 위한 충분한 여유를 남겨두었습니다.

segments.src: That cushion has thinned dramatically.
segments.tr: 그 쿠션이 극적으로 얇아졌습니다.

segments.src: And because shareholder return programs have not been cut proportionally, the gap has to be filled somewhere.
segments.tr: 그리고 주주 환원 프로그램이 비례해서 줄어들지 않았기 때문에, 그 격차는 어디선가 메워져야 합니다.

segments.src: It is being filled with debt.
segments.tr: 그 갭은 부채로 채워지고 있습니다.

segments.src: ## $194 billion in six months
segments.tr: ## 6개월 동안 1,940억 달러

segments.src: Market tallies of investment-grade issuance suggest technology and communications issuers sold on the order of **$194 billion of investment-grade bonds in the first half of 2026 alone** — a pace that would have been unthinkable for this sector five years ago, when several of these firms carried net cash positions and issued debt mainly for opportunistic or tax reasons.
segments.tr: 투자적격 등급 발행에 대한 시장 집계에 따르면 기술 및 통신 발행사들은 **2026년 상반기에만 약 1,940억 달러의 투자적격 채권을 발행**한 것으로 나타났습니다. 이는 이들 기업 중 여러 곳이 순현금 상태를 유지하고 주로 기회주의적 목적이나 절세 이유로 채권을 발행했던 5년 전만 해도 상상할 수 없었던 속도입니다.

segments.src: Roughly **a third of the capex program is being funded with borrowed money**.
segments.tr: **설비투자 프로그램의 약 3분의 1이 차입금으로 조달**되고 있습니다.

segments.src: That is a structural shift, not a one-quarter anomaly.
segments.tr: 이는 단기적인 아노말리가 아니라 구조적인 변화입니다.

segments.src: It changes what these companies are, financially speaking: from self-funding compounders into capital-intensive builders with a maturity schedule to manage.
segments.tr: 재무적으로 볼 때, 이는 이들 기업의 본질을 스스로 자금을 조달하는 복리 성장 기업에서 만기 일정을 관리해야 하는 자본 집약적 건설자로 변화시킵니다.

segments.src: ## Why borrow when you have the cash?
segments.tr: ## 현금이 있는데 왜 차입할까?

segments.src: There are several defensible reasons, and they are worth separating from the alarming interpretation.
segments.tr: 여기에는 우려스러운 해석과 구분하여 살필 만한 몇 가지 타당한 이유가 있습니다.

segments.src: **Asset-liability matching.** Data centers, substations, and land are long-lived assets.
segments.tr: **자산-부채 만기 일치.** 데이터 센터, 변전소, 토지는 수명이 긴 자산입니다.

segments.src: Funding a 20-year asset with 10- or 30-year debt is textbook corporate finance, not recklessness.
segments.tr: 20년짜리 자금을 10년 또는 30년 만기 부채로 조달하는 것은 교과서적인 기업 재무 기법이며 무모한 행동이 아닙니다.

segments.src: Chips are a different story — their useful life is contested, and that is where the argument gets interesting.
segments.tr: 반도체는 다른 이야기입니다. 유용한 수명에 대한 논란이 있으며, 바로 이 지점에서 논쟁이 흥미로워집니다.

segments.src: **Preserving flexibility.** Cash on the balance sheet is optionality: for acquisitions, for buybacks during a drawdown, for weathering a bad year.
segments.tr: **유연성 보존.** 재무상태표의 현금은 옵션성입니다. 인수합병, 시장 하락 시 자사주 매입, 어려운 해를 견뎌내기 위한 것입니다.

segments.src: Draining it to zero to fund construction would leave these firms more fragile, not less.
segments.tr: 건설 자금을 대기 위해 현금을 0으로 고갈시키는 것은 이 기업들을 더 견고하게 만드는 것이 아니라 더 취약하게 만들 것입니다.

segments.src: **The math still works — for now.** Investment-grade borrowers with strong ratings can raise long-term money at rates that remain below their expected return on invested capital, at least on the projections underpinning these programs.
segments.tr: **수학은 여전히 성립합니다 — 아직까지는.** 우수한 신용등급을 가진 투자적격 차입자는 적어도 이 프로그램들을 뒷받침하는 추정에 기반했을 때, 투자가본수익률보다 낮게 유지되는 금리로 장기 자금을 조달할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: If the projections hold, leverage is accretive.
segments.tr: 추정치가 유지된다면 레버리지는 이익을 증대시킵니다.

segments.src: **Tax and jurisdictional mechanics.** Interest is deductible; repatriating and deploying cash is not always frictionless.
segments.tr: **세금 및 관할권 메커니즘.** 이자는 공제 가능하며, 해외 현금을 본국으로 환수하여 투입하는 것이 항상 원활한 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: The optimization here is mundane and legitimate.
segments.tr: 이러한 최적화는 흔하고 정당한 절차입니다.

segments.src: The honest summary is that borrowing to build is a normal thing for a capital-intensive industry to do.
segments.tr: 솔직한 요약은 건설을 위해 차입하는 것이 자본 집약적 산업에서는 일반적인 일이라는 것입니다.

segments.src: What is new is that *this* industry is now capital-intensive.
segments.tr: 새로운 점은 *이* 산업이 이제 자본 집약적이 되었다는 사실입니다.

segments.src: ## What bond investors have started pricing in
segments.tr: ## 채권 투자자들이 가격에 반영하기 시작한 것

segments.src: Credit markets have absorbed the supply, but not for free.
segments.tr: 채권 시장은 공급을 흡수했지만, 공짜는 아니었습니다.

segments.src: A few dynamics are visible in how the debt is trading and how it is being structured:
segments.tr: 부채가 어떻게 거래되고 구성되는지에서 몇 가지 역학을 확인할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Concentration risk in the index.** As tech issuance grows, passive investment-grade funds are mechanically taking on more exposure to a single, highly correlated theme. An investor who bought a broad IG bond fund for diversification may now hold a meaningful bet on AI infrastructure economics.
segments.tr: – **지수 내 집중 위험.** 테크 기업의 채권 발행이 증가함에 따라 패시브 투자적격 펀드는 단일의 상호관련성이 높은 테마에 기계적으로 더 많이 노출되고 있습니다. 다변화를 위해 광범위한 IG 채권 펀드를 매수한 투자자는 이제 AI 인프라 경제성에 의미 있는 베팅을 보유하고 있을 수 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Modest spread differentiation.** Not all hyperscaler paper trades alike. Investors are increasingly distinguishing between issuers based on the visibility of the revenue that is supposed to service the debt, and on how much of the capex is committed versus discretionary.
segments.tr: – **완만한 스프레드 차별화.** 모든 하이퍼스케일러 채권이 동일하게 거래되는 것은 아닙니다. 투자자들은 부채를 상환하기로 되어 있는 매출의 가시성과 설비투자 중 얼마나 확정되어 있는지 대 재량에 맡겨져 있는지에 따라 발행사를 점점 더 구별하고 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Curve preference.** Demand has been noticeably firmer at shorter and intermediate maturities than at the very long end, where investors are being asked to underwrite the durability of AI demand two and three decades out.
segments.tr: – **수익률 곡선 선호도.** 투자자들이 20~30년 후의 AI 수요 지속 가능성을 보증해야 하는 초장기물보다는 단기 및 중기 만기물에서 수요가 확연히 더 강했습니다.

segments.src: - **Structures beyond plain bonds.** A growing share of the build is being financed through joint ventures, special-purpose vehicles, private credit, and long-dated leases. These are not necessarily problematic, but they make headline balance-sheet leverage an incomplete picture of total obligations.
segments.tr: – **일반 채권 이외의 구조.** 건설의 점점 더 큰 비중이 합작투자(JV), 특수목적법인(SPV), 사모펀드 대출, 장기 리스를 통해 조달되고 있습니다. 이것들이 반드시 문제가 되는 것은 아니지만, 헤드라인 재무상태표 레버리지만으로는 전체 채무의 완전한 그림을 파악하기 어렵게 만듭니다.

segments.src: That last point matters most for anyone trying to size the risk.
segments.tr: 마지막 포인트는 위험의 규모를 측정하려는 모든 이에게 가장 중요합니다.

segments.src: The bond market number is the visible part.
segments.tr: 채권 시장의 숫자는 눈에 보이는 부분입니다.

segments.src: The full financing footprint — including off-balance-sheet and partner-funded structures — is larger and harder to measure from the outside.
segments.tr: 부채외 거래 및 파트너 자금 조달 구조를 포함한 전체 자금 조달 발자국은 더 크며 외부에서 측정하기가 더 어렵습니다.

segments.src: ## The case for concern
segments.tr: ## 우려의 근거

segments.src: Three things would have to be true for this to end badly, and none of them are far-fetched.
segments.tr: 상황이 안 좋게 끝나려면 세 가지가 사실이어야 하며, 그 중 어느 것도 터무니없는 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: Depreciation assumptions prove optimistic.** Several firms extended the assumed useful life of server equipment in recent years, which lowers reported depreciation and flatters earnings.
segments.tr: 감가상각 가정이 낙관적임으로 판명됩니다.** 최근 몇 년 동안 여러 기업이 서버 장비의 예상 유용한 수명을 연장하여 보고되는 감가상각비를 낮추고 이익을 부풀렸습니다.

segments.src: If AI accelerators are functionally obsolete faster than the schedules assume, reported profits have been borrowing from the future — and the debt raised against those profits does not adjust.
segments.tr: AI 가속기가 일정보다 기능적으로 더 빠르게 구식화된다면, 보고된 이익은 미래에서 빌려온 것이며 이러한 이익을 담보로 늘린 부채는 조정되지 않습니다.

segments.src: Revenue attaches more slowly than capacity is added.** Capacity is being built ahead of demand by design; that is what an infrastructure race looks like.
segments.tr: 수용 능력이 추가되는 것보다 매출 확보가 더 더디게 이루어집니다.** 설계상 용량은 수요보다 앞서 구축되고 있으며, 이것이 인프라 경쟁의 모습입니다.

segments.src: But the gap between spend and monetization is currently being financed.
segments.tr: 그러나 지출과 수익화 사이의 격차는 현재 자금 조달로 메워지고 있습니다.

segments.src: A prolonged gap turns a growth story into a refinancing problem.
segments.tr: 장기화된 격차는 성장 스토리를 리파이낸싱 문제로 변모시킵니다.

segments.src: Rates or spreads move against them at the wrong moment.** These are strong credits with real cash flow.
segments.tr: 부적절한 시점에 금리나 스프레드가 불리하게 움직입니다.** 이들은 실질적인 현금 흐름을 가진 우량한 신용체입니다.

segments.src: But the maturity walls being created now will be refinanced under conditions nobody can forecast, and the assumption that IG tech will always find a bid is untested at this volume.
segments.tr: 그러나 지금 만들어지는 만기 벽은 아무도 예측할 수 없는 조건하에서 리파이낸싱될 것이며, IG 테크 채권이 항상 매수세를 찾을 것이라는 가정은 이 정도 규모에서 검증된 적이 없습니다.

segments.src: ## The case for calm
segments.tr: ## 차분함을 유지해야 할 근거

segments.src: The counterargument is not weak.
segments.tr: 반론 역시 약하지 않습니다.

segments.src: Leverage ratios at most of these issuers remain low by any historical corporate standard — net debt to EBITDA figures that a utility or telecom operator would consider enviable.
segments.tr: 이들 발행사 대부분의 레버리지 비율은 과거 기업 기준에 비추어 볼 때 여전히 낮습니다. 즉 유틸리티나 통신 사업자가 부러워할 만한 EBITDA 대비 순부채 수치입니다.

segments.src: Interest coverage is extraordinary.
segments.tr: 이자보상배율은 이례적으로 높습니다.

segments.src: The businesses funding the interest payments — cloud, advertising, enterprise software — are among the most durable cash engines ever built, and they are still growing.
segments.tr: 이자 지급을 뒷받침하는 사업들—클라우드, 광고, 엔터프라이즈 소프트웨어—은 지금까지 만들어진 가장 견고한 현금 엔진 중 일부이며 여전히 성장하고 있습니다.

segments.src: There is also a real asset at the end of this.
segments.tr: 또한 이 끝에는 실물 자산이 존재합니다.

segments.src: Unlike the fiber build of the late 1990s, which produced capacity that sat dark for years, much of today's compute is being consumed on delivery.
segments.tr: 수년간 유휴 상태로 방치된 용량을 생산했던 1990년대 후반의 광통신망 구축과 달리, 오늘날 컴퓨팅의 대부분은 제공되는 즉시 소비되고 있습니다.

segments.src: Utilization, where companies disclose it, has generally been high.
segments.tr: 기업들이 공개하는 가동률은 전반적으로 높은 수준을 유지해 왔습니다.

segments.src: The reasonable position is neither "this is a bubble financed with debt" nor "these companies can afford anything."
segments.tr: 합리적인 입장은 "이것은 부채로 조달된 거품이다"도 아니고 "이 기업들은 무엇이든 감당할 수 있다"도 아닙니다.

segments.src: It is that the risk profile of an entire sector has changed, and the market is in the middle of repricing it in real time.
segments.tr: 전체 섹터의 위험 프로필이 변경되었으며, 시장은 실시간으로 그 가격을 재산정하는 과정에 있다는 것입니다.

segments.src: ## What to actually watch
segments.tr: ## 실제로 주시해야 할 사항

segments.src: For readers tracking this rather than trading it, a handful of indicators carry more signal than headline capex numbers:
segments.tr: 트레이딩보다는 이를 추적하는 독자들에게는 헤드라인 설비투자 숫자보다 다음의 몇 가지 지표가 더 많은 신호를 제공합니다.

segments.src: - **Free cash flow, not operating cash flow.** Operating cash flow tells you the business is healthy. Free cash flow tells you what is left after the build.
segments.tr: – **영업현금흐름이 아닌 잉여현금흐름.** 영업현금흐름은 사업이 건전하다는 것을 알려줍니다. 잉여현금흐름은 건설 후 남은 것을 알려줍니다.

segments.src: - **Changes to depreciation schedules** disclosed in filings — an extension of useful life is a quiet earnings adjustment.
segments.tr: – 공시에서 공개되는 **감가상각 일정의 변경** — 유용한 수명의 연장은 조용한 이익 조정입니다.

segments.src: - **The ratio of committed to discretionary capex.** Discretionary spend can be cut in a downturn; contractual commitments cannot.
segments.tr: – **확정 설비투자 대 재량 설비투자의 비율.** 재량 지출은 침체 시 줄일 수 있지만 계약상의 의무는 줄일 수 없습니다.

segments.src: - **Spread behavior at issuance.** Whether new deals price with a concession relative to existing paper is the market's live verdict.
segments.tr: – **발행 시 스프레드 동작.** 신규 발행 건이 기존 채권 대비 할인된 가격에 정해지는지 여부가 시장의 생생한 판정입니다.

segments.src: - **Disclosure of JV, SPV, and lease obligations**, which increasingly sit outside the headline debt figure.
segments.tr: – **JV, SPV 및 리스 채무의 공시**, 이는 헤드라인 부채 수치 외부에 점점 더 많이 위치합니다.

segments.src: - **Any sign that shareholder return programs are being trimmed** — that would be management signaling the cash math has gotten tighter than guidance implies.
segments.tr: – **주주 환원 프로그램이 축소되고 있다는 모든 징후** — 이는 경영진이 현금 계산이 안내치보다 타이트해졌음을 알리는 신호일 것입니다.

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 요약

segments.src: The AI build-out is being financed the way large infrastructure has always been financed: with other people's money, on long timelines, against projected demand.
segments.tr: AI 인프라 구축은 대형 인프라가 항상 조달되어 온 방식대로 조달되고 있습니다. 즉 타인의 자금으로, 장기에 걸쳐, 예상 수요를 바탕으로 이루어집니다.

segments.src: That is not scandalous.
segments.tr: 그것은 충격적인 일이 아닙니다.

segments.src: It is simply a different business model than the one investors got used to, with a different set of failure modes.
segments.tr: 그것은 단지 투자자들이 익숙했던 것과는 다른 비즈니스 모델이며, 다른 유형의 고장 모드를 가지고 있을 뿐입니다.

segments.src: The companies that were famous for having no debt now have a maturity schedule.
segments.tr: 부채가 없는 것으로 유명했던 기업들에게 이제 만기 일정이 생겼습니다.

segments.src: Whether that turns out to be prudent capital allocation or an expensive lesson depends on a question nobody can answer yet — whether the revenue arrives on the same timeline as the interest payments.
segments.tr: 이것이 신중한 자본 배분으로 끝날지, 아니면 비싼 교훈으로 끝날지는 아무도 아직 답할 수 없는 질문, 즉 매출이 이자 지급과 동일한 일정으로 도착하는지 여부에 달려 있습니다.

segments.src: *This article is general information and commentary on publicly reported market data.
segments.tr: *본 기사는 공개 보고된 시장 데이터에 대한 일반적인 정보 및 해설입니다.

segments.src: Figures cited are estimates drawn from company disclosures and market tallies and may be revised.
segments.tr: 인용된 수치는 기업 공시 및 시장 집계에서 추출한 추정치이며 수정될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: It is not investment advice, and it is not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.
segments.tr: 투자 자문이 아니며, 어떠한 증권의 매수 또는 매도 추천도 아닙니다.

segments.src: Consult a qualified financial professional before making investment decisions.*
segments.tr: 투자 결정을 내리기 전에 자격을 갖춘 금융 전문가와 상담하십시오.*

zh.title: 大科技公司如今借贷建设：隐藏 exaggeration AI 繁荣背后的债券账单

segments.src: For most of the past two decades, the defining financial fact about America's largest technology companies was how much money they had lying around.
segments.tr: 在过去二十年的大部分时间里，关于美国最大科技公司最明确的财务事实是，它们手中拥有多少闲置资金。

segments.src: Cash piles measured in the hundreds of billions became a running joke on earnings calls and a genuine policy question in Washington.
segments.tr: 数以千计的现金堆积成了财报电话会议上的常用笑话，也成为了华盛顿关注的实质性政策问题。

segments.src: The companies were so liquid that the main debate was what to do with the surplus: buy back stock, pay dividends, or park it offshore.
segments.tr: 这些公司的流动性如此之高，以至于主要争议在于如何处理盈余：回购股票、支付股息，还是将其存放于海外。

segments.src: That framing is quietly going out of date.
segments.tr: 这种观念正在悄然过时。

segments.src: The build-out of artificial intelligence infrastructure has turned the most cash-generative businesses in the world into some of the largest borrowers in the corporate bond market — not because they are short of money, but because even their extraordinary cash flow no longer covers the bill.
segments.tr: 人工智能基础设施的建设已将世界上最赚钱的企业变成了企业债券市场中最大的借款人之一——这并不是因为 LinkedIn 或他们缺乏资金，而是因为即便他们拥有非凡的现金流，也无法再覆盖这笔账单了。

segments.src: ## The scale of the spend
segments.tr: ## 支出规模

segments.src: Estimates compiled from company guidance and analyst models put combined 2026 capital expenditure across the major hyperscalers at upward of **$750 billion**.
segments.tr: 根据公司指引和分析师模型汇总的估计，主要超大规模计算提供商在 2026 年的合计资本支出将达到 **7500 亿美元** 以上。

segments.src: To put that in perspective, it is a figure that would have described the entire capital spending of the S&P 500's industrial sector not long ago.
segments.tr: 直观来看，这一数字在不久前足以概括标准普尔 500 指数整个工业部门的全年资本支出。

segments.src: The more revealing number is the ratio.
segments.tr: 更具启示性的数字是这个比例。

segments.src: That spending represents roughly **94% of the group's operating cash flow** — meaning almost every dollar these companies generate from running their existing businesses is being committed to building the next one.
segments.tr: 这一支出大约占到 **该群体运营现金流的 94%**——这意味着这些公司通过运营现有业务产生的几乎每一美元都被投入到了构建下一个业务中。

segments.src: Historically, big tech converted operating cash flow into free cash flow at a comfortable clip, leaving ample room for buybacks and dividends.
segments.tr: 在历史上，大型科技公司能以舒适的速度将运营现金流转化为自由现金流，为股票回购和股息留出了充足的空间。

segments.src: That cushion has thinned dramatically.
segments.tr: 而这一缓冲垫已大幅变薄。

segments.src: And because shareholder return programs have not been cut proportionally, the gap has to be filled somewhere.
segments.tr: 由于股东回报计划并未按比例削减，因此这个缺口必须在某些地方填补。

segments.src: It is being filled with debt.
segments.tr: 它正在通过债务来填补。

segments.src: ## $194 billion in six months
segments.tr: ## 六个月内达 1940 亿美元

segments.src: Market tallies of investment-grade issuance suggest technology and communications issuers sold on the order of **$194 billion of investment-grade bonds in the first half of 2026 alone** — a pace that would have been unthinkable for this sector five years ago, when several of these firms carried net cash positions and issued debt mainly for opportunistic or tax reasons.
segments.tr: 投资级债券发行的市场统计表明，仅在 **2026 年上半年，科技和通信发行人就发行了约 1940 亿美元的投资级债券**——这种速度在五年前对该行业来说是不可思议的，当时这些公司中有几家持有净现金头寸，发行债务主要是出于机会主义或税务原因。

segments.src: Roughly **a third of the capex program is being funded with borrowed money**.
segments.tr: 大约 **三分之一的资本支出计划是通过借款资金资助的**。

segments.src: That is a structural shift, not a one-quarter anomaly.
segments.tr: 这是一次结构性转变，而不是单季度的异常现象。

segments.src: It changes what these companies are, financially speaking: from self-funding compounders into capital-intensive builders with a maturity schedule to manage.
segments.tr: 从财务角度来看，这改变了这些公司的本质：从自我供资的复合增长者转变为需要管理到期日程的资本密集型建设者。

segments.src: ## Why borrow when you have the cash?
segments.tr: ## 手头有现金，为何还要借贷？

segments.src: There are several defensible reasons, and they are worth separating from the alarming interpretation.
segments.tr: 有几个合理的理由，值得将其与令人担忧的解读区分开来。

segments.src: **Asset-liability matching.** Data centers, substations, and land are long-lived assets.
segments.tr: **资产负债匹配。** 数据中心、变电站和土地都是长寿命资产。

segments.src: Funding a 20-year asset with 10- or 30-year debt is textbook corporate finance, not recklessness.
segments.tr: 用 10 年或 30 年期的债务为 20 年期资产提供资金是教科书式的公司金融操作，而非鲁莽之举。

segments.src: Chips are a different story — their useful life is contested, and that is where the argument gets interesting.
segments.tr: 芯片则是另一回事——它们的使用寿命存在争议，这也是讨论变得有趣的地方。

segments.src: **Preserving flexibility.** Cash on the balance sheet is optionality: for acquisitions, for buybacks during a drawdown, for weathering a bad year.
segments.tr: **保持灵活性。** 资产负债表上的现金是选择权：用于收购、用于在回购时逢低买入、用于度过不景气的一年。

segments.src: Draining it to zero to fund construction would leave these firms more fragile, not less.
segments.tr: 将其消耗殆尽来资助建设会使这些公司变得更加脆弱，而不是更加稳健。

segments.src: **The math still works — for now.** Investment-grade borrowers with strong ratings can raise long-term money at rates that remain below their expected return on invested capital, at least on the projections underpinning these programs.
segments.tr: **数学逻辑依然成立——至少目前如此。** 拥有高评级的投资级借款人能够以低于其预期投资资本回报率的利率筹集长期资金，至少在支撑这些计划的预测上是如此。

segments.src: If the projections hold, leverage is accretive.
segments.tr: 如果预测成立，杠杆作用就能增厚收益。

segments.src: **Tax and jurisdictional mechanics.** Interest is deductible; repatriating and deploying cash is not always frictionless.
segments.tr: **税务和管辖权机制。** 利息支出是可以扣税的；而将海外现金汇回并部署并不总是顺畅无阻的。

segments.src: The optimization here is mundane and legitimate.
segments.tr: 这里的优化是日常且合法的。

segments.src: The honest summary is that borrowing to build is a normal thing for a capital-intensive industry to do.
segments.tr: 坦率的总结是，借贷建设对于资本密集型行业来说是件正常的事。

segments.src: What is new is that *this* industry is now capital-intensive.
segments.tr: 新鲜的是，*这个* 行业现在变成了资本密集型行业。

segments.src: ## What bond investors have started pricing in
segments.tr: ## 债券投资者已开始定价的因素

segments.src: Credit markets have absorbed the supply, but not for free.
segments.tr: 信贷市场已经吸收了这些供应，但并非毫无代价。

segments.src: A few dynamics are visible in how the debt is trading and how it is being structured:
segments.tr: 从债务的交易方式和结构设计中可以看出几种动态：

segments.src: - **Concentration risk in the index.** As tech issuance grows, passive investment-grade funds are mechanically taking on more exposure to a single, highly correlated theme. An investor who bought a broad IG bond fund for diversification may now hold a meaningful bet on AI infrastructure economics.
segments.tr: – **指数中的集中度风险。** 随着科技公司债券发行的增长，被动型投资级基金正机械地增加对单一、高度相关主题的敞口。为了分散投资而购买广泛 IG 债券基金的投资者，现在可能对 AI 基础设施经济性做出了重大押注。

segments.src: - **Modest spread differentiation.** Not all hyperscaler paper trades alike. Investors are increasingly distinguishing between issuers based on the visibility of the revenue that is supposed to service the debt, and on how much of the capex is committed versus discretionary.
segments.tr: – **适度的利差分化。** 并非所有超大规模提供商的债券交易方式都相同。投资者越来越倾向于根据用于偿还债务的收入可见性，以及资本支出中有多少是承诺性的与自决性的，来区分不同的发行人。

segments.src: - **Curve preference.** Demand has been noticeably firmer at shorter and intermediate maturities than at the very long end, where investors are being asked to underwrite the durability of AI demand two and three decades out.
segments.tr: – **收益率曲线偏好。** 短期和中期到期债券的需求明显强于超长端，因为在超长端，投资者被要求承销未来二三十年 AI 需求的持久性。

segments.src: - **Structures beyond plain bonds.** A growing share of the build is being financed through joint ventures, special-purpose vehicles, private credit, and long-dated leases. These are not necessarily problematic, but they make headline balance-sheet leverage an incomplete picture of total obligations.
segments.tr: – **常规债券之外的结构。** 建设资金中越来越多的份额正在通过合资企业（JV）、特殊目的载体（SPV）、私募信贷和长期租赁进行融资。这些不一定有问题，但它们使得报表上的资产负债表杠杆率无法完整反映总债务。

segments.src: That last point matters most for anyone trying to size the risk.
segments.tr: 这最后一点对任何试图衡量风险的人来说最为重要。

segments.src: The bond market number is the visible part.
segments.tr: 债券市场上的数字只是可见的一部分。

segments.src: The full financing footprint — including off-balance-sheet and partner-funded structures — is larger and harder to measure from the outside.
segments.tr: 完整的融资脚印——包括表外和合作伙伴资助的结构——规模更大，也更难从外部衡量。

segments.src: ## The case for concern
segments.tr: ## 令人担忧的理由

segments.src: Three things would have to be true for this to end badly, and none of them are far-fetched.
segments.tr: 要让这种情况以糟糕结局告终，必须满足三个条件，而且其中任何一个都不是耸人听闻的。

segments.src: Depreciation assumptions prove optimistic.** Several firms extended the assumed useful life of server equipment in recent years, which lowers reported depreciation and flatters earnings.
segments.tr: 折旧假设被证明过于乐观。** 近年来，几家公司延长了服务器设备的预期使用寿命，这降低了报告的折旧费用并美化了盈利。

segments.src: If AI accelerators are functionally obsolete faster than the schedules assume, reported profits have been borrowing from the future — and the debt raised against those profits does not adjust.
segments.tr: 如果 AI 加速器在功能上比预定日程更快淘汰，那么报告的利润实际上是在向未来借用——而针对这些利润筹集的债务却不会自动调整。

segments.src: Revenue attaches more slowly than capacity is added.** Capacity is being built ahead of demand by design; that is what an infrastructure race looks like.
segments.tr: 收入增长慢于产能增加的速度。** 按设计，产能建设领先于需求；这就是基础设施竞赛的本质。

segments.src: But the gap between spend and monetization is currently being financed.
segments.tr: 但支出与变现之间的差距目前正通过融资来填补。

segments.src: A prolonged gap turns a growth story into a refinancing problem.
segments.tr: 长期存在的差距会将一个增长故事转变为再融资问题。

segments.src: Rates or spreads move against them at the wrong moment.** These are strong credits with real cash flow.
segments.tr: 利率或利差在错误的时间走向不利方向。** 这些都是拥有真实现金流的强劲信用主体。

segments.src: But the maturity walls being created now will be refinanced under conditions nobody can forecast, and the assumption that IG tech will always find a bid is untested at this volume.
segments.tr: 但现在创建的到期墙将在没人能预测的条件下进行再融资，并且关于 IG 科技债券总能找到买家的假设在这种规模下未经测试。

segments.src: ## The case for calm
segments.tr: ## 保持冷静的理由

segments.src: The counterargument is not weak.
segments.tr: 反驳的理由并不弱。

segments.src: Leverage ratios at most of these issuers remain low by any historical corporate standard — net debt to EBITDA figures that a utility or telecom operator would consider enviable.
segments.tr: 按照任何历史企业标准来看，这些发行人中大多数的杠杆率仍然很低——公用事业或电信运营商都会羡慕其净债务与 EBITDA 的比率。

segments.src: Interest coverage is extraordinary.
segments.tr: 利息保障倍数非常出众。

segments.src: The businesses funding the interest payments — cloud, advertising, enterprise software — are among the most durable cash engines ever built, and they are still growing.
segments.tr: 资助利息支付的业务——云服务、广告、企业软件——是打造出的最耐用的现金引擎之一，而且它们仍在增长。

segments.src: There is also a real asset at the end of this.
segments.tr: 此外，这一切的尽头是真实的资产。

segments.src: Unlike the fiber build of the late 1990s, which produced capacity that sat dark for years, much of today's compute is being consumed on delivery.
segments.tr: 与 20 世纪 90 年代末产生多年闲置产能的光纤建设不同，当今的大部分算力在交付时即被消耗。

segments.src: Utilization, where companies disclose it, has generally been high.
segments.tr: 在公司披露产能利用率的地方，通常都保持在较高水平。

segments.src: The reasonable position is neither "this is a bubble financed with debt" nor "these companies can afford anything."
segments.tr: 合理的立场既不是“这是一个靠债务资助的泡沫”，也不是“这些公司负担得起任何费用”。

segments.src: It is that the risk profile of an entire sector has changed, and the market is in the middle of repricing it in real time.
segments.tr: 而是整个行业的风险特征已经改变，市场正处于实时重新为其定价的过程中。

segments.src: ## What to actually watch
segments.tr: ## 真正需要关注的指标

segments.src: For readers tracking this rather than trading it, a handful of indicators carry more signal than headline capex numbers:
segments.tr: 对于跟踪此事件而非参与交易的读者来说，有几个指标比报头上的资本支出数字包含更多信号：

segments.src: - **Free cash flow, not operating cash flow.** Operating cash flow tells you the business is healthy. Free cash flow tells you what is left after the build.
segments.tr: – **自由现金流，而非运营现金流。** 运营现金流告诉你业务是否健康。自由现金流告诉你建设完成后还剩下什么。

segments.src: - **Changes to depreciation schedules** disclosed in filings — an extension of useful life is a quiet earnings adjustment.
segments.tr: – 财报中披露的 **折旧日程变更** ——延长使用寿命是一种隐蔽的盈利微调。

segments.src: - **The ratio of committed to discretionary capex.** Discretionary spend can be cut in a downturn; contractual commitments cannot.
segments.tr: – **承诺性资本支出与自决性资本支出的比例。** 自决性支出可以在低迷时期削减；契约性承诺则不能。

segments.src: - **Spread behavior at issuance.** Whether new deals price with a concession relative to existing paper is the market's live verdict.
segments.tr: – **发行时的利差表现。** 新交易定价相对于现有债券是否有让步，是市场的实时裁决。

segments.src: - **Disclosure of JV, SPV, and lease obligations**, which increasingly sit outside the headline debt figure.
segments.tr: – **合资企业（JV）、特设机构（SPV）和租赁债务的披露**，这些债务越来越多地处于报头债务数字之外。

segments.src: - **Any sign that shareholder return programs are being trimmed** — that would be management signaling the cash math has gotten tighter than guidance implies.
segments.tr: – **股东回报计划被削减的任何迹象** ——那将是管理层发出的信号，表明现金算术已比指引所暗示的更为紧绷。

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## 总结

segments.src: The AI build-out is being financed the way large infrastructure has always been financed: with other people's money, on long timelines, against projected demand.
segments.tr: AI 的大建设正在以大型基础设施一贯的融资方式进行：利用他人的资金、在漫长的光阴里，针对预测的需求进行融资。

segments.src: That is not scandalous.
segments.tr: 这并不令人震惊。

segments.src: It is simply a different business model than the one investors got used to, with a different set of failure modes.
segments.tr: 这只是与投资者习惯的模式不同的另一种商业模式，并伴随着一组不同的失效模式。

segments.src: The companies that were famous for having no debt now have a maturity schedule.
segments.tr: 曾经以零债务闻名的公司现在有了到期日程。

segments.src: Whether that turns out to be prudent capital allocation or an expensive lesson depends on a question nobody can answer yet — whether the revenue arrives on the same timeline as the interest payments.
segments.tr: 这最终会被证明是审慎的资本配置还是昂贵的教训，取决于一个目前没人能回答的问题——收入能否与利息支付在同一时间表中兑现。

segments.src: *This article is general information and commentary on publicly reported market data.
segments.tr: *本文仅供参考，是对公开市场数据的通用信息与点评。

segments.src: Figures cited are estimates drawn from company disclosures and market tallies and may be revised.
segments.tr: 文中引用的数字是根据公司披露和市场统计得出的估计值，可能会进行修订。

segments.src: It is not investment advice, and it is not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.
segments.tr: 本文不构成投资建议，也不构成买卖任何证券的推荐。

segments.tr: 在做出投资决策之前，请咨询合格的财务专业人员。*

hi.title: बिग टेक अब निर्माण के लिए कर्ज ले रहा है: AI बूम के पीछे छिपा बॉन्ड बिल

segments.src: For most of the past two decades, the defining financial fact about America's largest technology companies was how much money they had lying around.
segments.tr: पिछले दो दशकों के अधिकांश समय के लिए, अमेरिका की सबसे बड़ी प्रौद्योगिकी कंपनियों के बारे में सबसे बड़ा वित्तीय तथ्य यह था कि उनके पास कितना नकदी जमा था।

segments.src: Cash piles measured in the hundreds of billions became a running joke on earnings calls and a genuine policy question in Washington.
segments.tr: सैंकड़ों अरबों में मापी जाने वाली नकदी की ढेरियाँ अर्निंग कॉल्स पर हंसी-मजाक का विषय बन गईं और वाशिंगटन में एक वास्तविक नीतिगत प्रश्न बन गईं।

segments.src: The companies were so liquid that the main debate was what to do with the surplus: buy back stock, pay dividends, or park it offshore.
segments.tr: कंपनियां इतनी लिक्विड थीं कि मुख्य बहस यह थी कि अधिशेष (surplus) का क्या किया जाए: शेयर वापस खरीदें, लाभांश का भुगतान करें, या इसे विदेशी खातों में रखें।

segments.src: That framing is quietly going out of date.
segments.tr: वह सोच अब धीरे-धीरे पुरानी हो रही है।

segments.src: The build-out of artificial intelligence infrastructure has turned the most cash-generative businesses in the world into some of the largest borrowers in the corporate bond market — not because they are short of money, but because even their extraordinary cash flow no longer covers the bill.
segments.tr: आर्टिफिशियल इंटेलिजेंस इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर के निर्माण ने दुनिया के सबसे अधिक नकदी पैदा करने वाले व्यवसायों को कॉरपोरेट बॉन्ड बाजार में सबसे बड़े उधारकर्ताओं में से कुछ में बदल दिया है — इसलिए नहीं कि उनके पास पैसे की कमी है, बल्कि इसलिए कि उनका असाधारण कैश फ्लो भी अब इस बिल को पूरा नहीं कर पा रहा है।

segments.src: ## The scale of the spend
segments.tr: ## खर्च का पैमाना

segments.src: Estimates compiled from company guidance and analyst models put combined 2026 capital expenditure across the major hyperscalers at upward of **$750 billion**.
segments.tr: कंपनी के मार्गदर्शन और विश्लेषक मॉडल से संकलित अनुमानों के अनुसार प्रमुख हाइपरस्केलर्स का संयुक्त 2026 कैपिटल एक्सपेंडिचर (capex) **$750 billion** से अधिक हो गया है।

segments.src: To put that in perspective, it is a figure that would have described the entire capital spending of the S&P 500's industrial sector not long ago.
segments.tr: यदि इसे संदर्भ में रखें, तो यह एक ऐसा आंकड़ा है जो कुछ समय पहले तक S&P 500 के औद्योगिक क्षेत्र के पूरे पूंजीगत खर्च का वर्णन करता।

segments.src: The more revealing number is the ratio.
segments.tr: अधिक खुलासा करने वाली संख्या अनुपात (ratio) है।

segments.src: That spending represents roughly **94% of the group's operating cash flow** — meaning almost every dollar these companies generate from running their existing businesses is being committed to building the next one.
segments.tr: वह खर्च इस समूह के **ऑपरेटिंग कैश फ्लो के लगभग 94%** को दर्शाता है — जिसका अर्थ है कि ये कंपनियां अपने मौजूदा व्यवसायों को चलाने से जो भी डॉलर कमाती हैं, उसमें से लगभग हर डॉलर अगले व्यवसाय को बनाने के लिए लगाया जा रहा है।

segments.src: Historically, big tech converted operating cash flow into free cash flow at a comfortable clip, leaving ample room for buybacks and dividends.
segments.tr: ऐतिहासिक रूप से, बिग टेक ने ऑपरेटिंग कैश फ्लो को फ्री कैश फ्लो में आराम से बदला, जिससे बायबैक और लाभांश के लिए पर्याप्त गुंजाइश बची।

segments.src: That cushion has thinned dramatically.
segments.tr: वह सुरक्षात्मक कुशन अब नाटकीय रूप से पतला हो गया है।

segments.src: And because shareholder return programs have not been cut proportionally, the gap has to be filled somewhere.
segments.tr: और चूंकि शेयरधारक रिटर्न कार्यक्रमों में आनुपातिक रूप से कटौती नहीं की गई है, इसलिए इस अंतर को कहीं न कहीं से पूरा करना होगा।

segments.src: It is being filled with debt.
segments.tr: इसे कर्ज (debt) से भरा जा रहा है।

segments.src: ## $194 billion in six months
segments.tr: ## छह महीने में $194 billion

segments.src: Market tallies of investment-grade issuance suggest technology and communications issuers sold on the order of **$194 billion of investment-grade bonds in the first half of 2026 alone** — a pace that would have been unthinkable for this sector five years ago, when several of these firms carried net cash positions and issued debt mainly for opportunistic or tax reasons.
segments.tr: इन्वेस्टमेंट-ग्रेड जारी करने के बाजार आंकड़ों से पता चलता है कि प्रौद्योगिकी और संचार जारीकर्ताओं ने **केवल 2026 की पहली छमाही में ही $194 billion के इन्वेस्टमेंट-ग्रेड बॉन्ड** बेचे — एक ऐसी गति जो पांच साल पहले इस क्षेत्र के लिए अकल्पनीय होती, जब इनमें से कई फर्मों के पास शुद्ध नकदी की स्थिति थी और वे मुख्य रूप से अवसरवादी या कर कारणों से ऋण जारी करती थीं।

segments.src: Roughly **a third of the capex program is being funded with borrowed money**.
segments.tr: लगभग **capex कार्यक्रम का एक तिहाई हिस्सा उधार लिए गए पैसे से वित्त पोषित किया जा रहा है**।

segments.src: That is a structural shift, not a one-quarter anomaly.
segments.tr: यह एक संरचनात्मक बदलाव है, एक तिमाही का अपवाद नहीं।

segments.src: It changes what these companies are, financially speaking: from self-funding compounders into capital-intensive builders with a maturity schedule to manage.
segments.tr: वित्तीय दृष्टिकोण से यह इन कंपनियों के स्वरूप को बदलता है: स्व-वित्तपोषित कंपाउंडर्स से परिपक्वता अनुसूची (maturity schedule) को प्रबंधित करने वाले पूंजी-गहन बिल्डरों में।

segments.src: ## Why borrow when you have the cash?
segments.tr: ## जब आपके पास नकदी है तो उधार क्यों लें?

segments.src: There are several defensible reasons, and they are worth separating from the alarming interpretation.
segments.tr: इसके कई रक्षात्मक कारण हैं, और उन्हें खतरनाक व्याख्या से अलग करना उचित है।

segments.src: **Asset-liability matching.** Data centers, substations, and land are long-lived assets.
segments.tr: **एसेट-लायबिलिटी मैचिंग।** डेटा सेंटर, सबस्टेशन और भूमि दीर्घकालिक संपत्तियां हैं।

segments.src: Funding a 20-year asset with 10- or 30-year debt is textbook corporate finance, not recklessness.
segments.tr: 10- या 30-वर्षीय ऋण के साथ 20-वर्षीय संपत्ति का वित्तपोषण करना पाठ्यपुस्तक कॉरपोरेट वित्त है, लापरवाही नहीं।

segments.src: Chips are a different story — their useful life is contested, and that is where the argument gets interesting.
segments.tr: चिप्स एक अलग कहानी हैं — उनके उपयोगी जीवन पर विवाद है, और यहीं से तर्क दिलचस्प हो जाता है।

segments.src: **Preserving flexibility.** Cash on the balance sheet is optionality: for acquisitions, for buybacks during a drawdown, for weathering a bad year.
segments.tr: **लचीलापन बनाए रखना।** बैलेंस शीट पर नकदी एक विकल्प है: अधिग्रहण के लिए, मंदी के दौरान बायबैक के लिए, या खराब वर्ष का सामना करने के लिए।

segments.src: Draining it to zero to fund construction would leave these firms more fragile, not less.
segments.tr: निर्माण कार्य को वित्तपोषित करने के लिए इसे शून्य पर ले जाना इन फर्मों को अधिक मजबूत नहीं, बल्कि अधिक नाजुक बना देगा।

segments.src: **The math still works — for now.** Investment-grade borrowers with strong ratings can raise long-term money at rates that remain below their expected return on invested capital, at least on the projections underpinning these programs.
segments.tr: **गणित अभी भी काम कर रहा है — अभी के लिए।** मजबूत रेटिंग वाले इन्वेस्टमेंट-ग्रेड उधारकर्ता उन दरों पर दीर्घकालिक धन जुटा सकते हैं जो निवेशित पूंजी पर उनके अपेक्षित रिटर्न से नीचे रहते हैं, कम से कम इन कार्यक्रमों के आधारभूत अनुमानों पर।

segments.src: If the projections hold, leverage is accretive.
segments.tr: यदि अनुमान सही रहते हैं, तो उत्तोलन (leverage) लाभदायक है।

segments.src: **Tax and jurisdictional mechanics.** Interest is deductible; repatriating and deploying cash is not always frictionless.
segments.tr: **कर और अधिकार क्षेत्र की प्रणाली।** ब्याज कटौती योग्य है; नकदी को वापस लाना और तैनात करना हमेशा बाधा रहित नहीं होता है।

segments.src: The optimization here is mundane and legitimate.
segments.tr: यहां अनुकूलन सामान्य और वैध है।

segments.src: The honest summary is that borrowing to build is a normal thing for a capital-intensive industry to do.
segments.tr: ईमानदार सारांश यह है कि निर्माण के लिए उधार लेना पूंजी-गहन उद्योग के लिए एक सामान्य बात है।

segments.src: What is new is that *this* industry is now capital-intensive.
segments.tr: नया यह है कि *यह* उद्योग अब पूंजी-गहन हो गया है।

segments.src: ## What bond investors have started pricing in
segments.tr: ## बॉन्ड निवेशकों ने किस बात का मूल्य निर्धारण शुरू कर दिया है

segments.src: Credit markets have absorbed the supply, but not for free.
segments.tr: क्रेडिट बाजारों ने आपूर्ति को समाहित कर लिया है, लेकिन मुफ्त में नहीं।

segments.src: A few dynamics are visible in how the debt is trading and how it is being structured:
segments.tr: ऋण के कारोबार और इसे कैसे तैयार किया जा रहा है, इसमें कुछ गतिकी दिखाई देती है:

segments.src: - **Concentration risk in the index.** As tech issuance grows, passive investment-grade funds are mechanically taking on more exposure to a single, highly correlated theme. An investor who bought a broad IG bond fund for diversification may now hold a meaningful bet on AI infrastructure economics.
segments.tr: – **इंडेक्स में एकाग्रता का जोखिम (Concentration risk)।** जैसे-जैसे टेक जारीकरण बढ़ता है, पैसिव इन्वेस्टमेंट-ग्रेड फंड यांत्रिक रूप से एक ही, अत्यधिक सह-संबंधित विषय पर अधिक जोखिम ले रहे हैं। एक निवेशक जिसने विविधीकरण के लिए एक व्यापक IG बॉन्ड फंड खरीदा है, वह अब AI इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर इकोनॉमिक्स पर एक महत्वपूर्ण दांव लगा सकता है।

segments.src: - **Modest spread differentiation.** Not all hyperscaler paper trades alike. Investors are increasingly distinguishing between issuers based on the visibility of the revenue that is supposed to service the debt, and on how much of the capex is committed versus discretionary.
segments.tr: – **मामूली स्प्रेड भिन्नता।** सभी हाइपरस्केलर पेपर एक समान व्यापार नहीं करते हैं। निवेशक जारीकर्ताओं के बीच इस आधार पर अंतर कर रहे हैं कि उस राजस्व की दृश्यता कितनी है जो ऋण चुकाने के लिए है, और capex का कितना हिस्सा प्रतिबद्ध बनाम विवेकाधीन है।

segments.src: - **Curve preference.** Demand has been noticeably firmer at shorter and intermediate maturities than at the very long end, where investors are being asked to underwrite the durability of AI demand two and three decades out.
segments.tr: – **कर्व प्राथमिकता।** मांग बहुत लंबे छोर की तुलना में छोटी और मध्यम परिपक्वताओं पर ध्यान देने योग्य रूप से अधिक मजबूत रही है, जहां निवेशकों से दो और तीन दशक बाद AI मांग के स्थायित्व को अंडरराइट करने के लिए कहा जा रहा है।

segments.src: - **Structures beyond plain bonds.** A growing share of the build is being financed through joint ventures, special-purpose vehicles, private credit, and long-dated leases. These are not necessarily problematic, but they make headline balance-sheet leverage an incomplete picture of total obligations.
segments.tr: – **सादे बॉन्ड से परे संरचनाएं।** निर्माण का एक बढ़ता हुआ हिस्सा संयुक्त उद्यमों (JV), विशेष प्रयोजन वाहनों (SPV), निजी क्रेडिट और दीर्घकालिक पट्टों के माध्यम से वित्त पोषित किया जा रहा है। ये जरूरी नहीं कि समस्याग्रस्त हों, लेकिन वे हेडलाइन बैलेंस-शीट लेवरेज को कुल देनदारियों की एक अधूरी तस्वीर बनाते हैं।

segments.src: That last point matters most for anyone trying to size the risk.
segments.tr: वह अंतिम बिंदु जोखिम का आकार तय करने की कोशिश करने वाले किसी भी व्यक्ति के लिए सबसे अधिक मायने रखता है।

segments.src: The bond market number is the visible part.
segments.tr: बॉन्ड मार्केट का आंकड़ा दृश्यमान हिस्सा है।

segments.src: The full financing footprint — including off-balance-sheet and partner-funded structures — is larger and harder to measure from the outside.
segments.tr: पूरा वित्तपोषण पदचिह्न — जिसमें ऑफ-बैलेंस-शीट और पार्टनर-वित्त पोषित संरचनाएं शामिल हैं — बड़ा है और बाहर से मापना अधिक कठिन है।

segments.src: ## The case for concern
segments.tr: ## चिंता का पक्ष

segments.src: Three things would have to be true for this to end badly, and none of them are far-fetched.
segments.tr: इसके बुरे अंत के लिए तीन चीजें सच होनी होंगी, और उनमें से कोई भी दूर की कौड़ी नहीं है।

segments.src: Depreciation assumptions prove optimistic.** Several firms extended the assumed useful life of server equipment in recent years, which lowers reported depreciation and flatters earnings.
segments.tr: मूल्यह्रास (Depreciation) धारणाएं आशावादी साबित होती हैं।** कई फर्मों ने हाल के वर्षों में सर्वर उपकरणों के अनुमानित उपयोगी जीवन को बढ़ा दिया है, जिससे रिपोर्ट की गई मूल्यह्रास कम हो जाती है और कमाई बेहतर दिखती है।

segments.src: If AI accelerators are functionally obsolete faster than the schedules assume, reported profits have been borrowing from the future — and the debt raised against those profits does not adjust.
segments.tr: यदि AI त्वरक schedules की तुलना में तेज़ी से अप्रचलित हो जाते हैं, तो रिपोर्ट किए गए लाभ भविष्य से उधार ले रहे हैं — और उन लाभों के विरुद्ध उठाया गया ऋण समायोजित नहीं होता है।

segments.src: Revenue attaches more slowly than capacity is added.** Capacity is being built ahead of demand by design; that is what an infrastructure race looks like.
segments.tr: क्षमता जोड़े जाने की तुलना में राजस्व धीरे-धीरे जुड़ता है।** डिजाइन द्वारा मांग से आगे क्षमता बनाई जा रही है; इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर की दौड़ ऐसी ही दिखती है।

segments.src: But the gap between spend and monetization is currently being financed.
segments.tr: लेकिन खर्च और मुद्रीकरण के बीच का अंतर वर्तमान में वित्त पोषित किया जा रहा है।

segments.src: A prolonged gap turns a growth story into a refinancing problem.
segments.tr: एक लंबा अंतर एक विकास कहानी को पुनर्वित्त (refinancing) समस्या में बदल देता है।

segments.src: Rates or spreads move against them at the wrong moment.** These are strong credits with real cash flow.
segments.tr: गलत समय पर दरें या स्प्रेड उनके खिलाफ चले जाते हैं।** ये वास्तविक नकदी प्रवाह वाले मजबूत क्रेडिट हैं।

segments.src: But the maturity walls being created now will be refinanced under conditions nobody can forecast, and the assumption that IG tech will always find a bid is untested at this volume.
segments.tr: लेकिन अब जो परिपक्वता दीवारें (maturity walls) बनाई जा रही हैं, उनका पुनर्वित्त उन परिस्थितियों में किया जाएगा जिनका कोई भी अनुमान नहीं लगा सकता है, और यह धारणा कि IG टेक को हमेशा एक बोली (bid) मिलेगी, इस मात्रा में परीक्षण नहीं की गई है।

segments.src: ## The case for calm
segments.tr: ## शांति का पक्ष

segments.src: The counterargument is not weak.
segments.tr: विरोधी तर्क कमजोर नहीं है।

segments.src: Leverage ratios at most of these issuers remain low by any historical corporate standard — net debt to EBITDA figures that a utility or telecom operator would consider enviable.
segments.tr: इनमें से अधिकांश जारीकर्ताओं में लेवरेज अनुपात किसी भी ऐतिहासिक कॉरपोरेट मानक के अनुसार कम बना हुआ है — शुद्ध ऋण से EBITDA के आंकड़े जिन्हें एक उपयोगिता या टेलीकॉम ऑपरेटर ईर्ष्याजनक मानेगा।

segments.src: Interest coverage is extraordinary.
segments.tr: ब्याज कवरेज असाधारण है।

segments.src: The businesses funding the interest payments — cloud, advertising, enterprise software — are among the most durable cash engines ever built, and they are still growing.
segments.tr: ब्याज भुगतानों को वित्तपोषित करने वाले व्यवसाय — क्लाउड, विज्ञापन, एंटरप्राइज़ सॉफ़्टवेयर — अब तक बनाए गए सबसे टिकाऊ कैश इंजनों में से हैं, और वे अभी भी बढ़ रहे हैं।

segments.src: There is also a real asset at the end of this.
segments.tr: इसके अंत में एक वास्तविक संपत्ति भी है।

segments.src: Unlike the fiber build of the late 1990s, which produced capacity that sat dark for years, much of today's compute is being consumed on delivery.
segments.tr: 1990 के दशक के अंत के फाइबर निर्माण के विपरीत, जिसने वर्षों तक बेकार पड़ी क्षमता पैदा की, आज के अधिकांश कंप्यूट की खपत डिलीवरी पर ही हो रही है।

segments.src: Utilization, where companies disclose it, has generally been high.
segments.tr: उपयोग, जहां कंपनियां इसका खुलासा करती हैं, आम तौर पर उच्च रहा है।

segments.src: The reasonable position is neither "this is a bubble financed with debt" nor "these companies can afford anything."
segments.tr: समझदारी पूर्ण स्थिति न तो "यह ऋण से वित्तपोषित एक बुलबुला है" की है और न ही "ये कंपनियां कुछ भी वहन कर सकती हैं" की है।

segments.src: It is that the risk profile of an entire sector has changed, and the market is in the middle of repricing it in real time.
segments.tr: यह है कि पूरे क्षेत्र का जोखिम प्रोफाइल बदल गया है, और बाजार वास्तविक समय में इसका पुनर्मूल्यांकन करने के बीच में है।

segments.src: ## What to actually watch
segments.tr: ## वास्तव में क्या देखना है

segments.src: For readers tracking this rather than trading it, a handful of indicators carry more signal than headline capex numbers:
segments.tr: व्यापार करने के बजाय इसे ट्रैक करने वाले पाठकों के लिए, कुछ संकेतक हेडलाइन capex संख्याओं की तुलना में अधिक संकेत देते हैं:

segments.src: - **Free cash flow, not operating cash flow.** Operating cash flow tells you the business is healthy. Free cash flow tells you what is left after the build.
segments.tr: – **फ्री कैश फ्लो, ऑपरेटिंग कैश फ्लो नहीं।** ऑपरेटिंग कैश फ्लो आपको बताता है कि व्यवसाय स्वस्थ है। फ्री कैश फ्लो आपको बताता है कि निर्माण के बाद क्या बचा है।

segments.src: - **Changes to depreciation schedules** disclosed in filings — an extension of useful life is a quiet earnings adjustment.
segments.tr: – फाइलिंग में खुलासा किए गए **मूल्यह्रास शेड्यूल में बदलाव** — उपयोगी जीवन का विस्तार एक शांत कमाई समायोजन है।

segments.src: - **The ratio of committed to discretionary capex.** Discretionary spend can be cut in a downturn; contractual commitments cannot.
segments.tr: – **प्रतिबद्ध बनाम विवेकाधीन capex का अनुपात।** मंदी में विवेकाधीन खर्च में कटौती की जा सकती है; संविदात्मक प्रतिबद्धताओं में नहीं।

segments.src: - **Spread behavior at issuance.** Whether new deals price with a concession relative to existing paper is the market's live verdict.
segments.tr: – **जारी करने के समय स्प्रेड व्यवहार।** क्या नए सौदे मौजूदा पेपर की तुलना में रियायत के साथ कीमत तय करते हैं, यह बाजार का जीवंत फैसला है।

segments.src: - **Disclosure of JV, SPV, and lease obligations**, which increasingly sit outside the headline debt figure.
segments.tr: – **JV, SPV, और पट्टे की देनदारियों का प्रकटीकरण**, जो तेजी से हेडलाइन ऋण आंकड़े के बाहर बैठते हैं।

segments.src: - **Any sign that shareholder return programs are being trimmed** — that would be management signaling the cash math has gotten tighter than guidance implies.
segments.tr: – **शेयरधारक रिटर्न कार्यक्रमों में कटौती का कोई भी संकेत** — यह प्रबंधन का यह संकेत होगा कि नकदी का गणित मार्गदर्शन के संकेत से अधिक तंग हो गया है।

segments.src: ## The bottom line
segments.tr: ## मुख्य बात

segments.src: The AI build-out is being financed the way large infrastructure has always been financed: with other people's money, on long timelines, against projected demand.
segments.tr: AI निर्माण को उसी तरह से वित्त पोषित किया जा रहा है जैसे बड़े इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर को हमेशा वित्त पोषित किया गया है: अन्य लोगों के पैसे से, लंबी समय-सीमा पर, अनुमानित मांग के खिलाफ।

segments.src: That is not scandalous.
segments.tr: वह कोई चौंकाने वाली बात नहीं है।

segments.src: It is simply a different business model than the one investors got used to, with a different set of failure modes.
segments.tr: यह केवल उस मॉडल से एक अलग व्यवसाय मॉडल है जिसके निवेशक आदी हो गए थे, जिसमें विफलता के अलग-अलग तरीके शामिल हैं।

segments.src: The companies that were famous for having no debt now have a maturity schedule.
segments.tr: जो कंपनियां बिना किसी कर्ज के लिए प्रसिद्ध थीं, अब उनके पास एक परिपक्वता अनुसूची है।

segments.src: Whether that turns out to be prudent capital allocation or an expensive lesson depends on a question nobody can answer yet — whether the revenue arrives on the same timeline as the interest payments.
segments.tr: यह विवेकपूर्ण पूंजी आवंटन साबित होता है या एक महंगा सबक, यह एक ऐसे प्रश्न पर निर्भर करता है जिसका उत्तर अभी तक कोई नहीं दे सकता है — कि क्या राजस्व ब्याज भुगतानों की समान समय-सीमा पर आता है या नहीं।
